Click the motion trace to scrub the 3D replay. Red lines mark the five chosen anchor times. The event detector is an explicit rule; the neural model learns candidate scores. COM uses native model masses. Head and hand points are mesh centers; foot points are body origins. Derivatives use recorded frame timing and seven-frame smoothing. All observations are offline hindsight, not causal controller inputs.

100 generated references trained; all 20 development references available here. Near-boundary means a sufficient 2–12 cm geometric gap, not decision-criticality or successful physical passage. Clearance filtering uses geometric bounds and can abstain; zero filtered penetration is not learned safety. Full recorded frames support the labels; replay shows up to 60 poses at their recorded times. G1 meshes are simplified only for display. Candidates follow five motion-event times: endpoints plus three separated peaks. Kinematic contrast requires reference clearance and penetration of an artificial shortcut or held pose. Those alternatives have not been physically qualified; this is not demonstrated decision-criticality. Obstacles are the newly labelled primitives, not qualified furniture assets. Initial root xy and body-origin height normalization match training.
